question: For fixed BTC and ETH trade streams over one common day, does previous-tick grid alignment change measured joint log-price variation relative to overlapping-interval accumulation?
mechanism: Non-synchronous observation times can suppress or alter measured cross-asset co-movement; this is an observation mechanism, not evidence of diversification or lead-lag predictability.
first_action: Research role can select a one-day ETH official public trade-file acquisition through the observed catalogue, qualify file identity/time and bind hash before scanning prices. Reuse the existing BTC file; no new scheduler or route claim.
planned_partition: 2026-09-23 in the official UTC+08:00 daily partition; verify in downloaded file, do not infer solely from filename
exposure: BTC input previously exposed. New ETH acquisition and all subsequent reads are development, never holdout.
data_requirements: Exact target contracts, original timestamps and price units, UTC partition and common observed support
Same-millisecond event ordering or a frozen bound; no arbitrary first/last row selection
Source coverage and RPI segment semantics recorded; no use of funding rates as price
Qualified synchronous midquotes needed before attributing differences specifically to asynchrony rather than trade-price noise
minimal_experiment: After input qualification and method freeze, compare exactly one 60-second previous-tick grid with overlap-increment covariance on the same frozen support. Retain observation ages, counts and unmatched intervals. No lag, ticker, scale or threshold search.
baseline: Grid statistic G=sum(delta log BTC at grid * delta log ETH at grid). Previous tick is an explicit estimator transformation, never a claim of actual contemporaneous observations. No leading backfill or extrapolation beyond observed support.
comparison: H=sum(delta log BTC_i * delta log ETH_j) for intervals (t_i-1,t_i] and (s_j-1,s_j] with max(left)<min(right). Report H,G,H-G as dimensionless descriptive cumulative covariation, not the demeaned sample covariance used in Roll and not a correlation/beta.
boundary_rule: Freeze common observed support and grid anchor after timestamp-only audit, before price calculations. Keep and disclose endpoint censoring; do not insert unobserved boundary prices. Different prices at identical unsequenced timestamps stop point estimation until bounds or ordering are separately frozen.
counterevidence: Equal statistics within a predeclared numerical error bound fails to support alignment sensitivity on this day; a difference supports measurement dependence only. Neither result identifies true latent covariance or proves a diversification benefit.
completion: One qualified-input descriptive comparison with all frozen diagnostics and reproducible bytes, or a precise qualification failure. No trade plan or economic evaluation. Stop after the fixed comparison; no winner selection.
resources: One ETH daily archive, reuse ~19.5 MB BTC compressed file. ETH size, uncompressed memory and wall time UNKNOWN until file observation; timestamp audit first, ordered interval merge rather than Cartesian expansion.
restart: Initial acquisition/protocol qualification may proceed without new user approval. After a failure, retry only with corrected path/schema or new qualified evidence. After completion, only independent frozen sample, synchronized quotes or method correction can justify a new question.
cost_boundary: No trades or net-return estimate in diagnostic. Any later strategy requires full original allowed costs, funding, inventory and exit inputs. actual_net stays null; not an A/B gate.
